doc.title: Quincy Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Few Americans hold passports; Jones's constant travel
summary: Jones and Baker discuss how few Americans hold passports, the resulting isolationism, and Jones's nonstop travel to Beijing, Shanghai and Los Angeles.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: You once said on a concert that you couldn’t under- – that less than – I forget what the number was. Something like only about 10 or 15 percent of Americans even have a passport.
11. I remember you being astounded that other people were not – didn’t have this world view.

And only half of them use them. And the 25 percent of Congress and Senate, only half of them use them. So what it has done, David – I’m sorry to interrupt you – it’s caused – it’s created a kind of an isolationism in this country of not knowing and not caring what’s happening anyplace else. I’m just the opposite. I am so nosy. Sometimes I wish I didn’t even know or see or care, because it’s tedious. I travel like a 12-year-old. It’s sick. It really is.
Just coming back from Beijing, too.

Yeah, Beijing and Shanghai. In Los Angeles three days, and here. Get up the next morning to do Maya Angelou at 10 o’clock – 9 o’clock – 7 o’clock – and do the show at 9, and then all the other stuff that’s going on. It’s astounding.
